text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The 1,000-megawatt reactor number six at Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power plant will start operating as scheduled on November 12, after Bulgaria receives fresh nuclear fuel from Russia at the end of this week, said the acting chairman of the plant Kiril Kirilov. @

-- The central bank (BNB) is expected to discuss today ways to unblock four billion levs belonging to farm co-operatives' that were blocked in the nine banks put under special supervision by the central bank two weeks ago, BNB deputy governor Dimitar Dimitrov said.
-- Bulgaria has negotiatited the import of 120,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina due to be received in March and April, deputy agriculture minister Dimo Uzunov said.

-- Interior minister Nikolai Dobrev has proposed that all members of Bulgaria's parliament should have state or private bodyguards following the assasination of the former premier Andrei Lukanov last week, a socialist party official said.
-- Bulgaria's record high 300 percent main interest rate should be changed by the end of October, ecomomy minister Roumen Gechev said in the northern town of Pleven.
The rate should be either cut or raised to a new all-time high of 420 percent annually, he said.

-- Bulgaria's two largest trade unions plan a joint rally on October 15 to protest the economic and social policy of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's socialist government and its unability to tackle the country's acute crisis, union leaders said.

-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by some 10 billion levs to 81.85 billion levs at the end of September or 1.1 billion levs above the annual deficit target, finance ministry officials said. @

The sharp rise was mainly due to interest payments on the country's huge domestic debt and to budget revenues, blocked in the nine commercial banks put under special supervision on September 23 by the central bank.
-- Bulgarian women from villages near the Black Sea town of Bourgas sold their new born children in Greece for 2,000 German marks through a smuggling channel, sources from the prosecution said.

-- The International Monetary Fund could release a delayed second $115 million tranche to Bulgaria by the end of November if Sofia speeds up privatisation and mass sell-offs tenders, deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
